summary: Twelve comment-endorsed developer tools, privacy utilities, learning resources, services, and games from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Qwen Image 2.1
items.summary: An image-generation model with unusually strong small-text rendering and open weights.
items.why_included: A prompt-to-UI builder found its text fidelity best among current open-weight models.
items.evidence: The commenter praised Qwen Image 2.1's text rendering and small-text fidelity after comparative testing.

evidence_sources.author: jjcm
evidence_sources.excerpt: The text rendering definitely is much, much better than anything else on the open weights market right now. Small text fidelity is quite good.

items.name: stable-diffusion.cpp
items.summary: A C/C++ diffusion-model inference engine with day-one Qwen Image 2.1 support.
items.why_included: A user highlighted its immediate support for the newly released image model.
items.evidence: The commenter uses stable-diffusion.cpp and noted its day-one Qwen Image 2.1 support.

evidence_sources.author: nkhgfugjk
evidence_sources.excerpt: I am using sd.cpp, which is the cousin of llama.cpp:

items.name: uBlock Origin Lite for iOS
items.source_story_title: ChatGPT now knows what you do on other websites via ad collector
items.summary: A Safari content blocker that brings uBlock's lighter ruleset to iPhone and iPad.
items.why_included: A new user immediately regretted not installing the iOS blocker sooner.
items.evidence: The commenter had recently installed uBlock Origin Lite and strongly approved of the decision.

evidence_sources.author: consumer451
evidence_sources.excerpt: I finally got around to installing uBlock Origin Lite on iOS. I used to run the Firefox version on iOS, but that was discontinued long ago, and I never replaced it.  I feel like a bit of an idiot for not doing this sooner.

items.name: ntfy
items.source_story_title: Telling a Computer to Do Things
items.summary: An HTTP push-notification service for connecting scripts to phones and desktops.
items.why_included: A user described a practical ntfy-plus-Tasker automation loop on Android.
items.evidence: The commenter uses ntfy to trigger device actions including volume changes, OTP forwarding, and Syncthing resyncs.

evidence_sources.author: KetoManx64
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use ntfy to send commands from within scripts to my android devices.

items.name: DuckDB
items.source_story_title: Telling a Computer to Do Things
items.summary: An in-process analytical database whose REPL can inspect large JSON files directly.
items.why_included: A commenter identified it as a useful step beyond jq for massive JSON investigations.
items.evidence: The commenter expects DuckDB's JSON reader to help investigate files too large or awkward for jq.

evidence_sources.author: ccapitalK
evidence_sources.excerpt: This might actually be useful the next time I need to investigate a massive json file (`jq` can only go so far).

items.name: numpy-ts
items.summary: A TypeScript NumPy-style array library positioned as a fast WebAssembly-free option.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it as the faster path when avoiding WebAssembly.
items.evidence: The commenter said numpy-ts benchmarks faster than NumPy proper without requiring WebAssembly.

evidence_sources.author: bern4444
evidence_sources.excerpt: There is also numpy-ts[1] which is measured to be faster than numpy proper if you want to skip the webassembly.

items.name: birthday_party
items.summary: A GPU project for searching partial cryptographic hash collisions and chasing records.
items.why_included: Its author directly recommended it as an accessible spare-GPU challenge.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended partial hash-collision hunting and said the current record took about one GPU-day.

evidence_sources.author: Retr0id
evidence_sources.excerpt: If anyone else has spare GPU hours they don't know what to do with, may I recommend partial hash collisions:

items.name: Craftcloud
items.source_story_title: Sherline Tools Is Going Out of Business
items.summary: A marketplace comparing global quotes for outsourced 3D printing and CNC machining.
items.why_included: A repeat customer explicitly recommended it for finding suitable domestic print providers.
items.evidence: The commenter uses and recommends Craftcloud for comparing outsourced fabrication options.

items.name: Factoring RSA-260
items.summary: A technical account of porting CADO-NFS to GPUs for a large RSA factorization.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it as the more thorough explanation of the GPU factoring work.
items.evidence: The commenter explicitly recommended Cognition's article for its technical detail.

evidence_sources.author: bertonvv
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend reading their article since it's much more thorough on details.

items.name: Death — Open Yale Courses
items.source_story_title: Weeping whales: Stillborn humpback whale grieving documented
items.summary: A free Yale philosophy lecture series examining mortality, identity, and personal survival.
items.why_included: A commenter called the course great while linking a relevant identity lecture.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended Yale's free Death series as a useful treatment of personal identity.

evidence_sources.author: tenuousemphasis
evidence_sources.excerpt: There's a great free Yale lecture series called Death that goes into this.

items.name: Chrono Trigger
items.source_story_title: You can defeat the Dream Devourer from Chrono Trigger using an int overflow
items.summary: A classic time-travel JRPG whose 16-bit visuals and design still hold up.
items.why_included: A repeat player strongly endorsed its lasting quality across emulator and DS playthroughs.
items.evidence: The commenter said Chrono Trigger still holds up exceptionally well compared with later console games.

evidence_sources.author: cpburns2009
evidence_sources.excerpt: Chrono Trigger holds up very well, and much better than many PSX/N64 games. It was at the pinickle of 16bit sprite graphics.

items.name: Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup
items.source_story_title: An open source roguelike adventure through dungeons
items.summary: A free open-source roguelike with playable historical versions and evolving mechanics.
items.why_included: A returning player loved the version archive and preferred the current release.
items.evidence: The commenter praised access to every prior version and favored the current game.

evidence_sources.author: iamthemonster
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love that you can play every previous version for free too!  I THINK I like the current version the best
